stories.headline: FTSE 100 Rebounds 1.3% on Banks and Miners as the Flash PMI Shows Services Cooling
stories.summary: The FTSE 100 rose 134.48 points, or 1.30%, to 10,480.82 on Monday 23 Nov, led by banks, miners and Rolls-Royce (ad-hoc-news). S&P Global's flash composite PMI slipped to 52.3 in November from 52.9, as services eased to 52.0 from 52.8 while manufacturing held at 52.7.
stories.market: HSBC rose 3.24% and Barclays 3.65%; Anglo American gained 4.68%, Antofagasta 4.29% and Rolls-Royce 4.97% on 23 Nov.

body: London's blue-chip index closed at 10,480.82 on 23 Nov, up 1.30% from Friday's 10,346.34, after its worst week since March. Banks and miners, the biggest drags last week, led the recovery.

November's flash PMIs showed a softer services sector: the services activity index fell to 52.0 from 52.8, below expectations, while the composite eased to 52.3 from 52.9. Manufacturing stood at 52.7, with output the strongest since August 2024.

stories.headline: CAC 40 Regains 8,000 as Chipmakers Rebound, Even as November's Flash PMI Shows France's Private Sector Shrinking Faster
stories.summary: The CAC 40 closed 1.48% higher at 8,044.84 on Monday 23 Nov, recovering part of a 5.27% weekly loss, with STMicroelectronics up 8.96%. The rally came despite a flash November PMI for France that slipped to 46.2 from 46.6, further below the 50 line that separates growth from contraction.
stories.market: Industrials and steel led: ArcelorMittal rose 5.39%, Legrand 4.20% and Schneider Electric 4.11%, while Orange and TotalEnergies were the weakest large caps as Brent fell nearly 3%.

body: Paris shares climbed steadily through Monday's session. The CAC 40 was up 0.74% at 7,986 around midday, according to Zonebourse, and closed 1.48% higher at 8,044.84, back above 8,000 after a 5.27% drop the previous week.

Chip and industrial stocks did the work. STMicroelectronics rose 8.96% to EUR40.01, ArcelorMittal 5.39%, Legrand 4.20%, Schneider Electric 4.11% and Renault 4.06%. Orange (-1.55%), TotalEnergies (-0.90%) and Danone (-0.62%) were the main laggards.
The domestic data were weaker. France's flash November PMI fell to 46.2 from 46.6, extending the contraction, according to Zonebourse's midday report, even as equity markets across Europe recovered.

stories.headline: Intesa's EUR34.5 Billion Offer for Monte dei Paschi Enters Its Tender Phase After the MPS Board Calls the Price Fair
stories.summary: Intesa Sanpaolo's sweetened EUR34.5bn (about $38bn) offer for Monte dei Paschi di Siena is due to open to shareholders on Tuesday 24 Nov, after the MPS board said on Saturday 21 Nov that the price is financially fair but does not fully reflect the bank's prospective value, Reuters reported. Director Corrado Passera resigned late on 20 Nov over disagreements about the bid.
stories.market: MPS closed at EUR10.78 and Intesa at EUR5.901 on 20 Nov, both down more than 5% on the week; Intesa went ex-dividend (EUR0.22) on 23 Nov, and the BTP-Bund spread was just above 105bp at Monday's open.

body: Intesa's bid for MPS moves to shareholders this week. Intesa Sanpaolo's improved offer values Monte dei Paschi di Siena at EUR34.5bn, and the tender phase is due to begin on Tuesday 24 Nov, according to Reuters.

In its formal opinion released on Saturday 21 Nov, the MPS board said, based on its advisers' work, that the improved price was financially fair as of 18 Nov but did not fully capture the bank's future value. The board approved its position unanimously, though director Corrado Passera had resigned late on Friday 20 Nov over disagreements on the bid.

Both banks' shares fell in last week's broad sell-off: MPS closed at EUR10.78 and Intesa at EUR5.901 on 20 Nov, each down more than 5% over five days. Intesa detached a EUR0.22 interim dividend on 23 Nov. At Monday's open the FTSE MIB was down 0.83% at 48,299, weighed by dividend detachments, with the BTP-Bund spread just above 105bp and the 10-year BTP yield above 4.4%.

stories.headline: AEX Jumps 2.15% as ASML, BE Semiconductor and ASM International Each Rise More Than 8%
stories.summary: Amsterdam's AEX closed 2.15% higher on Monday 23 Nov, led by chip-equipment makers as the AI sell-off paused: BE Semiconductor rose 9.25% to EUR155.90, ASML 8.92% to EUR1,272.20 and ASM International 8.29% to EUR692.60, Investing.com reported. Advancers outnumbered decliners 71 to 26.
stories.market: Defensive information-services and telecom names lagged, with Wolters Kluwer down 2.33%, KPN 1.82% and RELX about 1.4%; the euro fell 0.73% to about $1.09.

body: The Dutch market, heavy in semiconductor equipment, was one of Europe's strongest on Monday 23 Nov. The AEX ended 2.15% higher, with technology, basic materials and industrials leading.

BE Semiconductor gained 9.25% to EUR155.90, ASML 8.92% to EUR1,272.20 and ASM International 8.29% to EUR692.60. At the other end, Wolters Kluwer fell 2.33% to EUR83.88, KPN 1.82% to EUR4.27 and RELX about 1.4% to EUR35.06.
The gains came hours before Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang set off a 6.5% jump in the Nasdaq Composite later on Monday, which points to further support for the chip names on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Russia's Tax Take Rises 11% to 54.6 Trillion Roubles in Ten Months as the MOEX Index Gains 1.2%
stories.summary: Russia collected 54.6tn roubles in taxes in January-October, up 11% on a year earlier, with non-oil and gas revenues up 24% as the main driver, according to figures prepared for a 23 Nov meeting between tax service head Daniil Egorov and President Vladimir Putin, TASS reported. The MOEX index rose 1.21% to 2,381.62 on Monday 23 Nov.
stories.market: The dollar-based RTS index rose 1.26% to 913.3; the central bank set the official dollar rate for 24 Nov at 82.1488 roubles, about 4 kopecks lower, and homebuilder Samolet led the MOEX with a 10.75% gain.

body: According to materials for a meeting between Federal Tax Service head Daniil Egorov and Vladimir Putin, reported by Russian state agency TASS on 23 Nov, total tax receipts reached 54.6tn roubles (about $666bn) in the first ten months of 2026, up 11%. Federal budget revenue rose by 2.2tn roubles (10.4%), with non-oil and gas income up 24%; regional budgets took in 17.5tn roubles, up 9.4%.

Energy income is recovering from a weak base. Reuters calculations reported on 20 Nov projected November oil and gas tax revenue at 770bn roubles, up 45% from a year earlier, though January-November receipts of 7.2tn roubles would still be 10% lower year on year against a full-year budget plan of 7.58tn.

Moscow stocks rose on Monday: the MOEX index gained 1.21% to 2,381.62 and the RTS 1.26% to 913.3, led by Samolet (+10.75%), VK (+5.86%) and gold miner Polyus (+5.26%). The Bank of Russia set official rates for 24 Nov at 82.1488 roubles per dollar, 90.2815 per euro and 12.2615 per yuan, each slightly stronger for the rouble.

stories.headline: Central Bank Weakens the Hryvnia to 45.08 per Dollar as an IMF Repayment Falls Due and the 2027 Budget Slips to December
stories.summary: The National Bank of Ukraine set the official rate for 24 Nov at 45.08 hryvnias per dollar and 49.46 per euro, weaker by 15 and 18 kopecks respectively, Finway reported. Ukraine has a SDR62.5m repayment to the IMF due on 24 Nov and SDR125.7m on 9 Dec, while the 2027 budget, originally due for a final vote this week, has been pushed to 7-10 Dec to allow more consultation with the IMF.
stories.market: Interbank quotes were 45.18/45.21 per dollar at 16:00 on 23 Nov; the hryvnia has lost about 8% against the dollar this year, and a combined IMF review could release about $1.67bn if approved.

body: The NBU weakened the official hryvnia rate for Tuesday 24 Nov to 45.08 per dollar and 49.46 per euro. On the interbank market at 16:00 on 23 Nov the dollar was quoted at 45.18/45.21. NBU Council member Vasyl Furman said on 14 Nov that a sharp devaluation had no economic basis and that the central bank covers the war-driven import gap by selling reserves; the hryvnia is down about 8% against the dollar this year.

Debt service is due at the same time. According to the IMF's online database, as reported by Russian state agency TASS on 24 Nov, Ukraine owes SDR62.5m to the Fund on 24 Nov and SDR125.7m on 9 Dec, with 2027 payments of about SDR1.49bn (more than $2bn).

Kyiv is also waiting on new money. An IMF mission began combined second and third reviews of Ukraine's $8.1bn Extended Fund Facility on 9 Nov, which could unlock about $1.67bn if the Executive Board approves it. Finance committee member Yaroslav Zhelezniak said the 2027 budget, which was due for a final vote during 23-26 Nov, will instead come up on 7-10 Dec to allow more coordination with the IMF and other partners.

stories.market: The MSCI Tadawul index edged down 0.23% to 1,350.21; Jarir Marketing fell 8.04% to SR15.68 while Gulf General Cooperative Insurance rose 9.83%.

Losses were narrower than on Sunday but still broad, with 178 stocks lower and 84 higher. The parallel Nomu market fell 1.79%. Saudi Printing and Packaging (-8.43%), Saudi Darb (-8.33%) and Jarir (-8.04%) were the biggest losers.

stories.headline: Egyptian Stocks Bounce 1.4% After Sunday's Rout as Local Buyers Absorb Foreign Selling
stories.summary: The EGX30 rose 1.44% to 50,711.96 on Monday 23 Nov, regaining 50,000 a day after a 2.85% slide that wiped EGP141.6bn off market value, and the EGX70 jumped 3.41% (Amwal Al Ghad; Middle East Observer). Egyptian investors were net buyers of about EGP2.41bn while non-Arab foreigners sold a net EGP2.45bn.
stories.market: Market capitalisation recovered to about EGP3.997trn; the central bank's dollar rate had risen to about EGP54.36-54.50 on Sunday from 53.74-53.88 on Thursday.

body: On Sunday 22 Nov the EGX30 fell 2.85% to 49,989.79, its fourth straight loss and first close below 50,000 since 3 Nov; the EGX70 dropped 5.55%, and 205 stocks fell against 4 risers. The day cost EGP141.6bn in market value, taking losses since 12 Nov to about EGP247bn.
Monday brought a rebound: the EGX30 rose 1.44% to 50,711.96 and the EGX70 3.41% to 17,098.16. Local investors bought a net EGP2.41bn while non-Arab foreigners were net sellers of EGP2.45bn.
The pound weakened about 1.2% against the dollar into Sunday, even as foreigners bought a net EGP45.36bn of Treasury bills in the secondary market the previous week.

stories.headline: Nigeria's MPC Decides Today With Analysts Leaning to a Hold at 23% as the Naira Slips Toward N1,390
stories.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria's Monetary Policy Committee ends its two-day meeting on Tuesday 24 Nov, with the policy rate at 23% after a 350bp cut in September and October inflation at a six-year low of 14.06% (ThisDay). Analysts including Uche Uwaleke expect a hold, citing renewed foreign-exchange pressure and pre-election dollar demand.
stories.market: The naira was about N1,389 per dollar on 23 Nov, from about N1,350 in September, and gross reserves slipped to US$54.6bn from US$55.25bn over the same period (ThisDay).

body: The CBN's rate-setters conclude their November meeting on 24 Nov. The policy rate stands at 23% after September's cut from 26.5%, with the standing-facilities corridor at +50/-300bp and banks' cash reserve requirement at 45%.

Headline inflation fell to 14.06% in October, the lowest in about six years, which keeps the door open to further easing. But the naira has weakened to about N1,389 per dollar and reserves have dipped to US$54.6bn, and analysts warn election-year spending could revive demand for dollars.
Uwaleke of the Institute of Capital Market Studies expects the committee to keep the rate, corridor and CRR unchanged, describing it as a deliberate pause rather than an end to easing.
detail.consensus: Analysts surveyed by ThisDay and BusinessDay mostly expect a hold at 23%.

stories.headline: Taiex Logs Its Biggest-Ever Intraday Point Gain, Up 9%, as Huang's Return to Nvidia Lifts TSMC to Limit-Up
stories.summary: The Taiex rose as much as 3,368.49 points (9.15%) on Tuesday 24 Nov, the largest intraday point gain on record, and stood at 40,141.76 (+9.05%) at 11:36 a.m. Taipei time, Focus Taiwan reported. The rebound followed Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, after a week in which the Taiex fell almost 18% and regulators imposed a ban on short sales below the previous close.
stories.market: TSMC opened at its 10% daily limit at NT$2,230 and alone added about 1,600 index points; MediaTek, ASE and Hon Hai also hit limit-up, and more than 500 stocks on the main board and OTC market rose 10%.

body: Taiwan's benchmark staged a record rebound in the Tuesday morning session. At 11:36 a.m. on 24 Nov the Taiex was up 3,329.87 points, or 9.05%, at 40,141.76, having earlier been up as much as 3,368.49 points (9.15%), according to Focus Taiwan. That is the largest intraday point gain in the index's history; in percentage terms it ranks second, behind a 9.39% jump on 10 April 2025.

The trigger came from the US. Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, and Nvidia shares rose about 31.5% on Monday 23 Nov, their largest one-day gain in 23 years. Huang had resigned on 12 Nov after reports about his private life, including an alleged relationship with a businesswoman that US authorities suspected of spying for China; Beijing denied the spying allegations. Dealers in Taipei said his return eased worries about the AI build-out without him.

TSMC, which makes up more than 40% of the market's value, opened at its 10% limit at NT$2,230 after its US-listed shares rose 14.08% overnight, and contributed roughly 1,600 points of the index gain. MediaTek (NT$4,050) and ASE Technology (NT$530) also hit the 10% limit, and the financial sub-index was up 8.96% at 11:36 a.m.

The rally comes after a historic rout: the Taiex lost almost 18% last week, its worst week since 1991, more than twice the Kospi's roughly 8% drop. A ban on short sales of any stock trading below its previous close took effect on Monday 23 Nov, when the index closed about 2% higher.

stories.headline: Kospi Jumps About 7% Back Above 5,000, Triggering a Buy Sidecar, Two Days Before an Expected Bank of Korea Hike
stories.summary: The Kospi rose 315.04 points (6.69%) to 5,023.58 by 11:20 a.m. KST on 24 Nov, reclaiming 5,000 a day after closing at 4,708.54, its lowest since 13 Jan, the Korea Times reported; a buy-side sidecar paused program buying at 9:06 a.m. A Reuters poll found 32 of 34 economists expect the Bank of Korea to raise its base rate to 3.25% from 3% on Thursday 26 Nov.
stories.market: Samsung Electronics rose about 7.7% and SK hynix about 8.5% in the morning; the won was 1,344.6 per dollar at 11:20 a.m., 2 won weaker on the day.

body: Seoul's market opened 3.64% higher on Tuesday 24 Nov and was up 6.69% at 5,023.58 by 11:20 a.m. KST, according to the Korea Times. The exchange activated a buy-side sidecar at 9:06 a.m., halting program buy orders for five minutes after Kospi 200 futures rose at least 5%. Chip heavyweights led: Samsung Electronics was up 7.72% and SK hynix 8.48% in the morning.

The jump reverses part of a brutal slide. The Kospi fell 5.2% on Friday 20 Nov and a further 3.3% to 4,708.54 on Monday 23 Nov, its lowest close since 13 Jan. Seoul has said it is ready to activate a stock-market stabilisation fund of about 10.8tn won, the first such step since the 2008 crisis; no activation had been confirmed as of Tuesday morning.

The rally coincides with a policy week: 32 of 34 economists in a Reuters poll expect the Bank of Korea under Governor Shin Hyun-song to raise the base rate by 25bp to 3.25% on Thursday, the highest since October 2024, after hikes in May and July. Third-quarter GDP grew 3.4% year on year against the central bank's 2.6% forecast, and October consumer inflation was 2.8%.

stories.headline: Nikkei Jumps About 4% as Tokyo Reopens and JGBs Rally; Flash PMI Keeps a December BOJ Hike in View
stories.summary: The Nikkei 225 rose 3.97% to 58,675.79 by the midday break on Tuesday 24 Nov, after briefly gaining about 5%, as Tokyo reopened from Monday's holiday into the AI-stock relief rally; Advantest rose nearly 14%, Reuters reported. November's flash PMI showed manufacturing at 53.7, with export orders the strongest since 2018, while S&P Global said persistent price pressure supports expectations of a Bank of Japan hike in December.
stories.market: The Topix gained about 2.5%; Japanese government bonds rallied, with the 10-year yield down about 8bp to roughly 2.70% and the 2-year about 5bp lower near 1.78%, while the dollar held near 159 yen.

body: Tokyo was shut for a holiday on Monday 23 Nov, so Tuesday was its first chance to trade Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang. The Nikkei was up 3.05% at 58,159.74 shortly after the open (about 00:10 GMT) and 3.97% higher at 58,675.79 at the midday break, having briefly risen about 5%. Chip-testing equipment maker Advantest rose nearly 14%.

The broader Topix rose about 2.5%. Bonds rallied at the same time: the 10-year JGB yield fell about 8bp to around 2.70% and the 2-year about 5bp to around 1.78%, according to investingLive's session wrap. The dollar was little changed near 159 yen.

S&P Global's flash November PMI showed manufacturing rising to 53.7, with export orders the strongest since 2018, while services slowed to 50.5 and business optimism matched its lowest since 2020. S&P Global said lingering price pressures support expectations that the BOJ will raise rates in December.

stories.headline: ASX 200 Snaps an Eight-Day Losing Streak, Up 1.6%, as Tech and Miners Rally; ANZ Pushes Its First RBA Cut to 2027
stories.summary: The S&P/ASX 200 was up 139.6 points (1.63%) at 8,710.2 at 3:32 p.m. AEDT on 24 Nov, on track to end an eight-session losing streak, after closing 0.25% lower at 8,570.6 on Monday, IBTimes Australia reported. Ten of 11 sectors rose, with materials up 2.3%; ANZ moved its forecast for the first Reserve Bank rate cut to June 2027 from November, citing a weakening labour market.
stories.market: Reliance Worldwide (+11.9%), GQG Partners (+10.2%) and Lovisa (+9%) led gains while energy names Santos and Ampol lagged as Brent slid; the Australian dollar was little changed near 66.3 US cents.

body: Australian shares tracked Wall Street's rebound on Tuesday 24 Nov. ASX 200 futures were up 1.5% by 9:15 a.m., and by 3:32 p.m. AEDT the index was up 1.63% at 8,710.2, according to IBTimes Australia, after Monday's 0.25% fall to 8,570.6. The Small Ordinaries rose 2.4%.

Ten of 11 sectors advanced. Technology led, materials rose 2.3%, real estate 1.6% and consumer discretionary 1.3%, while energy lagged as Brent fell to about US$89-90 a barrel. Among individual stocks, Reliance Worldwide rose 11.92% to A$5.07, GQG Partners 10.19% and Lovisa 9% to A$26.16.

ANZ moved its forecast for the RBA's first rate cut to June 2027 from November 2026, citing a softening jobs market, and now expects three cuts taking the cash rate to 4.10% by February 2028. The RBA raised the cash rate to 4.85% on 3 Nov; October monthly CPI is due on Wednesday.

stories.headline: Jakarta Stocks Open 1.3% Higher as Bank Indonesia Says MSCI Talks With Prabowo Support the Rupiah
stories.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index opened 1.29% higher at 5,283.29 on Tuesday 24 Nov, from Monday's close of 5,215.85, Fortune Indonesia reported. On Monday the rupiah hit a record low of 18,290 per dollar before recovering to as strong as 18,180, and Bank Indonesia said remarks by MSCI chief Henry Fernandez in talks with President Prabowo raised hopes for the stock market, Reuters reported.
stories.market: MSCI has warned Indonesian stocks could be removed from its indexes in 2027 and possibly cut two steps to 'standalone' status; Bloomberg reported Fernandez signalled openness to alternatives to that downgrade on a 10 Nov call.

body: Indonesian equities opened firmer on 24 Nov, with the Jakarta Composite up 1.29% at 5,283.29 at the open and the blue-chip LQ45 up 1.42% at 547.87, according to Fortune Indonesia.

The currency had a volatile Monday. The rupiah touched a record low of 18,290 per dollar on 23 Nov and then strengthened to as much as 18,180 by 07:33 GMT, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters. Bank Indonesia's Erwin Gunawan Hutapea said remarks by MSCI chief executive Henry Fernandez had created positive expectations for the stock market.

Bloomberg reported that on a 10 Nov call brokered by Bridgewater founder Ray Dalio, Fernandez signalled willingness to consider alternatives to a two-step downgrade of Indonesia from emerging-market to 'standalone' status. MSCI has warned the market could be removed from its indexes in 2027; Reuters could not independently verify the Bloomberg report.

stories.headline: KSE-100 Climbs More Than 1,200 Points at the Open on the Global AI Relief Rally
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 rose 1,231.49 points (0.69%) to 178,705.34 by 9:45 a.m. PKT on 24 Nov, Business Recorder reported, after a flat Monday close of 177,473.86 (+0.05%). Banks, fertiliser, oil and gas explorers and power producers led, with HUBCO, OGDC, PPL, MARI and HBL among the gainers.
stories.market: The rupee was 276.70 per dollar in the interbank market on 23 Nov; Standard Chartered expects the State Bank's policy rate could rise to 13% by June 2027.

body: Karachi joined the regional rebound in early trade on Tuesday 24 Nov. The KSE-100 was at 178,705.34 at 9:45 a.m., up 1,231.49 points or 0.69%, after a range-bound Monday that ended just 91.29 points higher at 177,473.86 on negative breadth and lower turnover.

Buying spread across automobile assemblers, commercial banks, fertiliser, exploration and production, oil marketing and power generation, with HUBCO, ARL, MARI, OGDC, PPL, POL, HBL, MEBL, MCB and UBL trading higher.

The backdrop was Monday's 31.5% jump in Nvidia after Jensen Huang's reinstatement, which lifted Asian markets on Tuesday. At home, the government cut petrol prices by Rs3 a litre while keeping diesel unchanged, and Standard Chartered sees the State Bank's policy rate possibly reaching 13% by June 2027.

stories.headline: Sri Lankan Bond Yields Climb After the Rate Hike as Foreigners Sell for a Fifth Week and Stocks Slip 0.6%
stories.summary: Sri Lankan government bond yields rose 5-20bp on Monday 23 Nov, with the 2030 bond at 11.30/35% from 11.10/20%, in the first session after the central bank's 25bp rate hike and one-point rise in the reserve ratio on 20 Nov, EconomyNext reported. Foreign investors sold a net Rs8.6bn ($26m) of rupee bonds in the latest week, a fifth straight week of outflows.
stories.market: The All Share index fell 0.60% to 21,242.52 on turnover of Rs1.05bn, with Dilmah Ceylon Tea down 10.4%; the rupee closed at 332.55/60 per dollar, from 332.60/65.

body: Colombo's debt market repriced on Monday 23 Nov. The bond maturing in August 2030 closed at 11.30/35%, up from 11.10/20%, and the 2036 bond at 12.35/40% from 12.25/30%, EconomyNext reported. The rupee was steady at 332.55/60 per dollar, though it had lost 6.9% this year as of 13 Nov.

The move follows the Central Bank of Sri Lanka's decision on Friday 20 Nov to raise its policy rate by 25bp and lift the statutory reserve ratio by one percentage point, which Governor Nandalal Weerasinghe said would absorb about Rs150bn of roughly Rs460bn in excess liquidity. He projected headline inflation near 9% by end-November, above the 7% upper target band, and a return to target in the second half of 2027.

Foreign holders keep selling: net outflows from rupee bonds were Rs8.6bn ($26m) in the week to 18-19 Nov and Rs42.5bn over seven weeks. Equities also eased, with the All Share index down 0.60% at 21,242.52 and the S&P SL20 down 0.34% at 6,054.76.
